definition_zh: 大胆的；粗体的；鲜明的
definition_en: brave and confident enough to take risks
core_image: 会议室里第一个站起来发言的人
scene: 他在会上第一个站起来反对。 It was a bold move to speak first at the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 bold 是「大胆的」（第 1 个义项：敢于冒险、不怕后果）；句意是在会上第一个发言是个大胆的举动。

pos.zh: 形容词：大胆的；粗体的；鲜明的

derivatives.zh: 大胆地，勇敢地

senses.title: Brave and confident
senses.definition: willing to take risks and say what you think
senses.definitionCN: 愿意冒险并敢于说出自己的想法
senses.example: It was a bold move to speak first at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 在会上第一个发言是个大胆的举动。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, naming a person who is not afraid.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，指无所畏惧的人。

senses.title: Thick and dark in print
senses.definition: printed with thick dark lines that stand out

senses.why: A bold person stands out, and thick letters were seen the same way.
senses.whyCN: 大胆的人很显眼，粗重的字母也同样显眼。

senses.title: Strong and easy to see
senses.definition: strong and clear in colour or shape

senses.example: She painted the wall in bold colours.
senses.exampleCN: 她把墙刷成了鲜明的颜色。
senses.why: Anything that forces the eye to stop was called bold.

definition_zh: 生物技术
definition_en: the use of living things to make products or solve problems
core_image: 实验室里一排培养皿泛着微光
scene: 实验室里一排培养皿在灯下泛光。 Biotechnology has changed medicine.
sceneCN: 这里 biotechnology 是「生物技术」（第 1 个义项：利用生物体制造产品或解决问题）；句意是生物技术改变了医学。

pos.zh: 名词：生物技术；生物技术学

derivatives.zh: biotechnology 的缩略形式，义为「生物技术」

由 biotechnology 加 -ist 构成，义为「生物技术专家」

senses.title: Using life to make products
senses.definition: the industrial use of living things
senses.definitionCN: 利用生物体进行工业生产
senses.example: Biotechnology has changed medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 生物技术改变了医学。
senses.why: This is the working sense, covering drugs, crops and materials.
senses.whyCN: 这是实用义，涵盖药物、作物与材料。

senses.title: The field of study
senses.definition: the academic subject that studies such methods
senses.definitionCN: 研究这类方法的学科
senses.example: She teaches biotechnology at the college.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这所学院教生物技术。
senses.why: Any technology also becomes a subject taught in schools.
senses.whyCN: 任何技术也会成为学校里的课程。

intro.en: Biotechnology is a twentieth-century compound of bio and technology.
intro.cn: biotechnology 是二十世纪由 bio 与 technology 合成的词。

items.en: the word named farming and fermentation methods.
items.cn: 这个词先指农业与发酵方法。

items.en: microbiology gave the term new weight.
items.cn: 微生物学让这个词更有分量。

items.en: gene methods created a new industry.
items.cn: 基因技术催生新产业。

items.en: biotech became a common short form.
items.cn: biotech 成为常见简称。

items.en: the term covers medicine, food and energy.
items.cn: 如今这个词涵盖医药、食品与能源。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ology pattern; the near-meaning group gives related fields.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ology 结构；近义组是相关领域。

entries.definition: the use of scientific knowledge
the study of living things
the story of a person's life

normalIntro.cn: biotechnology 就是把生物学用到工业上去。

normal.en: Biotech is the everyday short form.

normal.en: The word is uncountable as a field.

normal.en: A biotechnologist works in the field.

normal.cn: 形容词是 biotechnological。

normal.en: The word joins bio, life, with technology.

abstract.en: See a green field grown from new seed.

sensesIntro.en: The industry and the classroom subject carry the same long name.
sensesIntro.cn: 产业与课堂上的学科，共用这个长长的名字。

definition_zh: 高效地；不浪费时间地；以高产出的方式
definition_en: in a way that uses little time or energy for the work done, by a well-planned method, or with high output for the input
core_image: 仓库里货架重排，取货的人少走一半路
scene: 仓库把货架重新排过，取货的人少走了一半的路。 Goods now move efficiently from shelf to van.
sceneCN: 这里 efficiently 是「高效地」（第 1 个义项：用较少时间与力气完成同样的活）；句意是货物现在从货架到货车都走得很高效。

pos.zh: 副词：高效地；不浪费时间地；以高产出的方式

forms.label: 比较级（副词，多音节用 more）
最高级（副词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到，义为「高效的」
由 efficient 加 -ency 构成，义为「效率」
由 efficient 加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「低效的」

senses.title: Without wasted effort
senses.definition: in a way that uses little time, energy or material for the work done
senses.definitionCN: 以较少的时间、精力或材料完成所做工作的方式
senses.example: Goods now move efficiently from shelf to van.
senses.exampleCN: 货物现在从货架到货车都走得很高效。
senses.why: -ly turns efficient into a manner: the work is finished and little is spent doing it.
senses.whyCN: -ly 把 efficient 变成方式：活干完了，而干的过程中花得很少。

senses.title: By a well-planned method
senses.definition: by an organized method in which each step follows the last without doubling back
senses.definitionCN: 以有条理的方法进行，每一步接上一步，不来回折返
senses.example: The whole event was efficiently run.
senses.exampleCN: 整场活动办得有条不紊。
senses.why: An organized schedule removes wasted motion, so efficiently also describes the order of the steps.
senses.whyCN: 有条理的日程去掉了多余的走动，所以 efficiently 也描述步骤的先后顺序。

senses.title: With high output for the input
senses.definition: of a machine or system, producing a large useful output compared with what is supplied
senses.definitionCN: 指机器或系统，与投入相比产出很多有用的东西
senses.example: The pump runs efficiently at low speeds.
senses.exampleCN: 这台泵在低速下也运转得很高效。
senses.why: For machines, doing well is measured as output over input, and the adverb reports that ratio.
senses.whyCN: 对机器来说，干得好要用产出除以投入来衡量，而这个副词报告的正是那个比值。

intro.en: Efficiently is English efficient plus -ly, with the stem going back through French to Latin efficiens.
intro.cn: efficiently 是英语 efficient 加 -ly，词干经法语上溯到拉丁语 efficiens。

items.en: Ex- out plus facere formed efficere, to accomplish.
items.cn: 表示「出」的 ex- 加 facere 构成 efficere，意为「完成」。

items.en: The participle described something as accomplishing or producing.
items.cn: 分词描述某物正在完成或正在产生。

items.en: French kept the adjective with the sense of producing a result.
items.cn: 法语保留这个形容词，意思是「能产生结果的」。

items.en: English applied it to machines, methods and people who waste little.
items.cn: 英语把它用于机器、方法与很少浪费的人。

items.en: The adverb -ly carried the same idea into how an action is performed.
items.cn: 副词 -ly 把同一个意思带进「动作如何进行」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the efficiency family; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of smooth and productive action.
note.cn: 形近组收 efficiency 词族；近义组收表示顺畅、多产地行动的副词。

entries.definition: Working well without waste, or able to produce a result.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「高效的」，是本词的词基。

entries.definition: The quality of working without waste, or the output-to-input ratio.
In a way that succeeds, or in practice; it stresses the result, not the saving.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「有效地、实际上」，强调结果而不强调省。

entries.definition: Without trouble or interruption; it stresses flow rather than economy.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「顺利地」，强调顺畅而非节省。

entries.definition: In a way that yields a good amount of work or output.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「多产地」，强调产出量。

entries.definition: In a way that saves money or resources.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「节约地」，强调省钱省资源。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow a shorter walk in a warehouse, then a well-run day and a pump that gives more than it takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着仓库里缩短的一段路，再走到井井有条的一天与一台「产出多过消耗」的泵。

normal.en: Efficiently means fewer steps for the same delivery.
normal.cn: efficiently 就是用更少的步子完成同样的送货。

normal.en: A reordered shelf can cut a warehouse walk in half.
normal.cn: 重排一次货架，就能把仓库里的走动砍掉一半。

normal.en: An efficiently run event has no one waiting for someone else.
normal.cn: 办得有条理的活动，没有人干等另一个人。

normal.en: For a pump, efficiently means output divided by input.
normal.cn: 对泵来说，efficiently 就是产出除以投入。

normal.en: Efficient is what it is; efficiently is how it is done.
normal.cn: efficient 说的是它什么样；efficiently 说的是它怎么做。

abstract.en: Picture a warehouse where every shelf sits where the picker turns first.
abstract.cn: 想象一座仓库，每排货架都正好在取货人转身就能到的地方。

abstract.en: The goods travel the same distance in the end, but the walk is shorter.
abstract.cn: 货物最终走的距离没变，但人走的路短了。

abstract.en: Efficiently is that shorter walk written as an adverb.
abstract.cn: efficiently 就是把那段更短的路写成一个副词。

examples.en: Goods now move efficiently from shelf to van.
examples.cn: 货物现在从货架到货车都走得很高效。

examples.cn: 整场活动办得有条不紊。

examples.en: The pump runs efficiently at low speeds.
examples.cn: 这台泵在低速下也运转得很高效。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of efficiently: without wasted effort, by a well-planned method, and with high output for the input.
sensesIntro.cn: efficiently 的三个义项：不浪费力气、按有条理的方法、以高产出对投入的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shelves reordered so the picker walks half as far.
core.cn: 核心意象：货架重排后，取货人少走一半路。

branches.en: THE WASTE: the same work costs less time and energy.
branches.cn: 浪费线：同样的活花费更少的时间与精力。

branches.en: THE ORDER: each step follows the one before without doubling back.
branches.cn: 顺序线：每一步接上一步，不来回折返。

branches.en: THE RATIO: a machine gives much for what is supplied.

definition_zh: 糊状物；酱；面团；粘贴；痛打
definition_en: a soft wet mixture such as crushed food or an adhesive; also to stick something onto a surface, or in informal use to beat someone badly
core_image: 碗里一团湿润的糊被抹刀挑起，稳稳贴到另一面上去
scene: 厨房的案板上摊着一层细腻的糊，厨师用刀背把它抹平，再盖上一张薄纸。 She mixed the flour with water until it formed a thick paste.
sceneCN: 这里是「糊状物」（第 1 个义项：柔软湿润的混合物）；句意是她把面粉和水搅成浓稠的糊。画面里有案板、抹刀和一只盛水的碗。

derivatives.zh: 由 paste 加 -y 构成，形容面色像糊一样苍白
由 paste 加 -ry 构成，指用面团烤成的糕点
由 tooth 与 paste 复合而成，指牙膏
由 paste 与 up 复合而成，指拼贴成的版面

senses.title: A soft, wet mixture
senses.definition: a soft wet substance made by crushing or mixing materials together
senses.definitionCN: 把材料碾碎或混合后形成的柔软湿润的物质
senses.example: Add a spoonful of tomato paste to the sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 往酱汁里加一勺番茄酱。
senses.why: The word came in as the name of dough, and dough is the first picture of a soft mass, so any soft mass can take the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是「面团」的名字，而面团就是柔软一团的最初画面，于是任何柔软的糊状物都能沿用这个称呼。

senses.title: Dough for pastry
senses.definition: a mixture of flour, fat and liquid, rolled out and baked into pastry
senses.definitionCN: 面粉、油脂与液体混合后擀开、烤成糕点用的面团
senses.example: The cook rolled the paste thin before cutting out the shapes.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师把面团擀薄，再切出各种形状。
senses.why: In older cooking, paste meant the dough itself, and that sense still lives in the names of baked goods made from it.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的烹饪语境里，paste 指的就是面团本身，这层意思至今还留在用面团做成的糕点名称里。

senses.title: To stick something onto a surface
senses.definition: to fix paper or another material onto a surface with paste or glue; also to place copied text or an image in a document
senses.definitionCN: 用浆糊或胶水把纸张等材料固定在某个表面上；也指把复制的文字或图像放进文档里
senses.example: She pasted the photograph into the middle of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 她把照片粘到了页面的正中。
senses.why: Once the noun names the sticky mixture, the verb naturally names the act of using it, and the computer menu extended that act to text and images.
senses.whyCN: 名词既指有黏性的糊，动词自然就指使用这种糊的动作；电脑菜单又把这个动作延伸到文字和图像上。

senses.title: To beat someone badly
senses.definition: to hit someone hard and repeatedly, or to defeat them easily, in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中指狠狠地连打某人，或轻易击败对手
senses.example: The champion pasted his opponent in the second round.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军在第二回合把对手打得毫无还手之力。
senses.why: This rough sense is a separate informal development: hitting something until it flattens is imagined as pressing it into a paste.
senses.whyCN: 这层粗鲁的意思来自另一条口语发展线：把对方打到像被压成糊一样，于是用 paste 来形容痛打。

intro.en: Paste reaches English from a Greek word for barley porridge, by way of Latin dough and a French noun for a sticky mixture.
intro.cn: paste 从希腊语表示大麦粥的词出发，经由拉丁语的「面团」和法语表示黏稠混合物的名词，才进入英语。

items.en: Greek paste meant a barley porridge, a soft mass of grain and liquid; the related adjective pastos meant sprinkled.
items.cn: 希腊语 pastē 指大麦粥，即谷物与液体混合成的软团；相关形容词 pastos 意为「撒过的」。

items.en: Latin pasta named dough or a small cake of dough, and it kept the picture of something kneaded and soft.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pasta 指面团或面团做的小饼，保留了「揉过的柔软之物」这一画面。

items.en: Old French paste carried both the dough sense and the sense of a sticky mixture used to make things adhere.
items.cn: 古法语 paste 既有面团的意思，也有用来黏合东西的糊状物之意。

items.en: Middle English paste covered dough, pastry and the glue made from flour and water.
items.cn: 中古英语的 paste 兼指面团、糕点，以及用面粉和水调成的浆糊。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb, the computing sense of inserting copied material, and the informal sense of beating someone.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了动词用法、把复制内容插入文档的计算机义，以及「痛打」的口语义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the dough family and its compounds; the near-meaning group collects sticky substances and soft food masses.
note.cn: 形近组收的是「面团」这一词族及其复合词；近义组收的是黏性物质与柔软的食品团块。

entries.definition: Italian food made from dough in many shapes.
entries.definitionCN: 用面团做成各种形状的意大利面食。

entries.definition: Dough baked with fat, or a sweet cake made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 加油脂烤成的面团，或用它做的甜点。

entries.definition: A folded pastry filled with meat or vegetables.
entries.definitionCN: 包着肉或蔬菜的折叠酥饼。

entries.definition: A soft substance used with a brush to clean teeth.
entries.definitionCN: 配合牙刷清洁牙齿的软膏状物。

entries.definition: A sticky liquid used to join materials together.
entries.definitionCN: 用来把材料黏合起来的黏稠液体。

entries.definition: A thick mixture of flour and liquid, ready to be baked.
entries.definitionCN: 面粉与液体混合、待烤的稠团。

entries.definition: A substance that makes two surfaces stick together.
entries.definitionCN: 使两个表面黏合的物质。

normalIntro.en: The word started as a name for soft dough and then spread to any soft mass, to glue, and to the act of sticking.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「柔软的面团」出发，随后扩展到任何柔软的团块、胶，以及把东西粘上去的动作。

normal.en: Paste and pastry share the dough stem, so a bakery and a glue pot are distant cousins.
normal.cn: paste 与 pastry 共用「面团」这个词干，因此面包房和浆糊罐是远亲。

normal.en: Toothpaste keeps the old sense: a soft mass that is squeezed out and spread.
normal.cn: toothpaste 保留了旧义：挤出来再抹开的柔软一团。

normal.en: Copy and paste borrows the kitchen action of pressing one thing onto another.
normal.cn: copy and paste 借用了厨房里把一样东西按到另一样上的动作。

normal.en: The verb is regular: pasted, pasted, pasting.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：过去式与过去分词都是 pasted，现在分词是 pasting。

normal.en: The informal sense of beating someone works by picturing the loser flattened like paste.
normal.cn: 口语里「痛打」的意思，是把输家想象成像糊一样被压扁。

abstract.en: Paste is matter that has given up its shape and can take any shape pressed into it.
abstract.cn: paste 是放弃了自身形状、可以被按成任何形状的物质。

abstract.en: Glue and dough are the same word because both are soft things that hold other things together.
abstract.cn: 胶与面团是同一个词，因为两者都是把别的东西黏住的软物。

abstract.en: A paste sits between solid and liquid, which is why the word slides so easily between food and glue.
abstract.cn: 糊处在固体与液体之间，所以这个词能在食物与胶之间轻易滑动。

examples.en: Stir the flour and water into a smooth paste.
examples.cn: 把面粉和水搅成细腻的糊。

examples.en: He pasted the two sheets of paper together with flour glue.
examples.cn: 他用面糊把两张纸粘在一起。

examples.en: A pat of almond paste makes a simple cake look finished.
examples.cn: 一小块杏仁膏就能让普通的蛋糕看起来完整。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩斯特」——把纸佩（贴）到墙上去；paste 就是粘贴。

root: 经古法语 paste 来自晚期拉丁语 pasta（面团），更早可追到希腊语 pastē（大麦粥）；同族词多与面团、糊状物有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a soft mass that can be spread or pressed; the senses divide into food masses, the sticky mixture, the act of sticking, and a rough slang use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是可以抹开或压扁的柔软一团；义项分出食品团块、黏稠的糊、粘贴的动作，以及一层粗俗的口语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of wet paste lifted on a knife and smoothed onto a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：抹刀挑起一团湿润的糊，把它在平面上抹平。

branches.cn: 一勺番茄酱搅进微沸的酱汁

branches.en: a rolling pin pressing dough into a thin sheet
branches.cn: 擀面杖把面团压成薄片

branches.en: a photograph fixed into the centre of a page
branches.cn: 一张照片被粘到页面正中

branches.en: a boxer flattened in the second round
branches.cn: 第二回合被打得毫无还手之力的拳手

branches.en: the same soft mass used as food and as glue
branches.cn: 同一团软物既当食物也当胶

intro.cn: 希腊语的粥、拉丁语的面团与法语表示黏稠混合物的名词，共同汇入这个简短的英语词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.

definition_zh: 适应；改编作品；生物适应
definition_en: the act of changing to fit, or a work changed for a new medium
core_image: 一本小说被摊开，旁边放着改好的分镜脚本
scene: 这一版改编把故事搬到了一座海边小镇。 This adaptation moves the story to a small seaside town.
sceneCN: 这里的 adaptation 是「改编作品」（第 2 个义项：为另一种媒介改写后的成品）；句中指这一版改写的电影。

pos.zh: 适应；改编作品；生物适应

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀还原为动词，义为「适应；改编」
加形容词后缀 -able，义为「能适应的」
由 adaptable 加 -ity，义为「适应性」
加表施动者的 -er，义为「适配器；改编者」

senses.title: The process of fitting in
senses.definition: the process of changing in order to deal with new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 为应对新条件而做出改变的过程
senses.example: Her adaptation to city life took several months.
senses.exampleCN: 她适应城市生活花了好几个月。
senses.why: The noun of adapt names the whole process, not a single change, which is why it often appears with to.
senses.whyCN: adapt 的名词指整个「变得合适」的过程，而不是某一次改动，所以常与 to 连用。

senses.title: A work rewritten for a new medium
senses.definition: a film, play or show made from a book or other source
senses.definitionCN: 根据书或其他来源改写的电影、戏剧或节目
senses.example: The film is a loose adaptation of a Russian novel.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影是对一部俄国小说的松散改编。
senses.why: When a book is fitted to the screen, the finished product itself came to be called an adaptation.
senses.whyCN: 当一本书被「装进」银幕，改出来的成品本身也就叫 adaptation。

senses.title: A trait that helps survival
senses.definition: a feature or behaviour that helps a living thing survive in its habitat
senses.definitionCN: 帮助生物在栖息地存活下来的身体特征或行为
senses.example: Thick fur is an adaptation to extreme cold.
senses.exampleCN: 厚厚的毛皮是对极寒的一种适应。
senses.why: Biology took the everyday word and made it name the result of fitting that evolution keeps.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了这个日常词，用来指进化保留下来的「贴合环境」的结果。

intro.en: The noun is the Latin action noun built on the verb meaning to fit to.
intro.cn: 这个名词是拉丁语里建立在「使适合」动词上的行为名词。

items.en: aptus meant fit or suitable.
items.cn: aptus 意为合适的、贴合的。

items.en: adaptare meant to fit one thing to another.
items.cn: adaptare 意为使一物贴合另一物。

items.en: adaptatio named the act of fitting.
items.cn: adaptatio 指「使贴合」这一行为。

items.en: adaptation carried the noun into French.
items.cn: adaptation 把这个名词带进法语。

items.en: English first used it for biology, then for rewritten plays.
items.cn: 英语先用它讲生物，后来才用它指改写的剧本。

note.en: The first group shares the adapt stem; the second names other results of fitting.
note.cn: 第一组共享 adapt 词干；第二组是别的表示「调整结果」的词。

normalIntro.en: adapt plus ation: the whole process, the finished work, and the trait that survives.
normalIntro.cn: adapt 加 ation：既是过程，也是成品，还是活下来的性状。

normal.en: The ending ation usually names an action or its result, as in creation.
normal.cn: ation 结尾通常指行为或其结果，如 creation。

normal.en: Film adaptation and stage adaptation are fixed phrases.
normal.cn: film adaptation 与 stage adaptation 是固定说法。

normal.en: In biology, adaptation is countable: one trait, two traits.
normal.cn: 在生物学里 adaptation 可数：一种性状，两种性状。

normal.en: Adaptation to is followed by the new condition.
normal.cn: adaptation to 后面接所适应新条件。

normal.en: The verb is adapt; do not drop the second a.
normal.cn: 动词是 adapt，别漏掉第二个 a。

abstract.en: See a marked-up novel beside a film storyboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一本写满批注的小说旁边放着电影分镜。

abstract.en: Picture a foreign student learning local table manners.
abstract.cn: 想象一位外国学生学当地的餐桌礼节。

abstract.en: Think of thick fur on an animal in deep snow.
abstract.cn: 想象厚雪里一只动物身上厚厚的毛。

examples.en: Adaptation to the new rules was slow at first.
examples.cn: 起初对新规则的适应很慢。

examples.en: The play is an adaptation of a famous diary.
examples.cn: 这出戏改编自一本著名日记。

examples.en: Long legs are an adaptation for running fast.
examples.cn: 长腿是跑得快的一种适应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿达普特申」——阿达把普特的小说改成剧本，申报时写的就是改编。

root: 拉丁语 adaptatio（使适合的行为），源自 adaptare（使贴合）与 aptus（合适的）；由「调整到相合」这一动作，兼指过程、成品与生物性状。

sensesIntro.en: One noun covers the process, the product and the trait.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词，同时指过程、成品与性状。

core.cn: 核心意象：小说与分镜并排放着。

branches.cn: 慢慢习惯一个新地方的过程

intro.cn: 一个表示「使贴合」的拉丁动词，加一个表行为的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: aptus also gives apt, aptitude and inept.
latinIntro.cn: aptus 还给出 apt、aptitude 与 inept。

definition_zh: 破产的；使破产；破产者
definition_en: unable to pay debts, or to make a person or company unable to pay
core_image: 空荡的店铺里只剩一张写着欠款的纸
scene: 街角的店关了门。 The company went bankrupt after the failed deal.
sceneCN: 这里 bankrupt 是「破产的」（第 1 个义项：无力偿还债务）；句意是那家公司在这笔交易失败后破产了。

pos.zh: 形容词：破产的；无力还债的

derivatives.zh: 由 bankrupt 加 -cy 构成，义为「破产」
由 bankrupt 加 -ing 构成，义为「使破产的行为」

senses.title: Unable to pay debts
senses.definition: legally unable to pay what one owes
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上无力偿还所欠债务
senses.example: The company went bankrupt after the failed deal.
senses.exampleCN: 那家公司在这笔交易失败后破产了。
senses.why: Bankrupt comes from Italian banca rotta, a broken bench, the sign that a money changer had failed.
senses.whyCN: bankrupt 来自意大利语 banca rotta「破掉的长凳」，那是钱商倒闭的标志。

senses.title: To ruin financially
senses.definition: to make a person or company unable to pay debts
senses.definitionCN: 使个人或公司无力偿还债务
senses.example: The lawsuit nearly bankrupted the family.
senses.exampleCN: 那场官司几乎让这个家庭破产。
senses.why: The adjective became a verb, so to bankrupt someone is to push them into that broken state.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为动词，所以 bankrupt someone 就是把对方推到那种破裂的境地。

intro.en: Bankrupt began as an Italian image of a broken bench.
intro.cn: bankrupt 起初是意大利语里「破掉的长凳」这一形象。

items.en: banca meant 'a bench' for money changers.
items.cn: banca 意为钱商用的「长凳」。

items.en: banca rotta meant 'a broken bench'.
items.cn: banca rotta 意为「破掉的长凳」。

items.en: the phrase named a failed money business.
items.cn: 这个说法指倒闭的钱庄。

items.en: English used it for a person who cannot pay.
items.cn: 英语用它指无力偿债的人。

items.en: bankruptcy is a legal status.
items.cn: 如今 bankruptcy 是一种法律状态。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bank- root; the near-meaning group gives words for ruin and debt.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bank 词根；近义组是破产与债务的说法。

definition_zh: 珍爱；珍惜；怀有
definition_en: to love and care for someone or something deeply, or to keep a hope or a memory in your mind
core_image: 双手捧着一件旧物贴在胸前
scene: 老人把泛黄的照片轻轻夹进书页。 She cherished the letter her grandmother had written.
sceneCN: 这里 cherish 指「珍爱」（第 1 个义项：深深爱惜并细心呵护）；句意是她珍爱祖母写的那封信。

derivatives.zh: 珍爱的；被珍视的
珍爱；呵护

senses.title: To love and protect
senses.definition: to love someone or something deeply and to treat it with care
senses.definitionCN: 深深爱着某人或某物，并小心对待
senses.example: He cherished the old watch his father left him.
senses.exampleCN: 他珍爱父亲留给他的那只旧表。
senses.why: The Old French source meant to hold dear, and holding dear easily becomes caring for.
senses.whyCN: 古法语词源意为「视为珍贵」，而视为珍贵很容易变成细心呵护。

senses.title: To keep in the mind
senses.definition: to keep a hope, idea or memory in your mind over a long time
senses.definitionCN: 长时间把某种希望、想法或记忆留在心里
senses.example: She cherished the hope of returning one day.
senses.exampleCN: 她怀着有朝一日回去的希望。
senses.why: What is dear is kept close, so the verb stretched from objects to hopes held inside.
senses.whyCN: 珍贵之物会被收在身边，于是动词从实物扩展到心里怀着的希望。

intro.en: Cherish comes from a Latin adjective meaning dear, through French verbs of holding dear.
intro.cn: cherish 源自拉丁语中表示「珍贵」的形容词，经法语中「视为珍贵」的动词传来。

items.en: Carus meant dear or beloved.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carus 意为珍贵的、被爱的。

items.en: Cher meant dear.
items.cn: 古法语 cher 意为珍贵的。

items.en: Cherir meant to hold someone or something dear.
items.cn: 古法语 cherir 意为把某人或某物视为珍贵。

items.en: Cherish meant to treat with tenderness and care.
items.cn: 英语 cherish 意为温柔小心地对待。

items.en: The verb also means to keep a hope or memory in the mind.
items.cn: 这个动词也指把希望或记忆留在心里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cher- opening, while the meaning group names strong affection.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cher- 开头，近义组列出强烈的喜爱之情。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the dear root carus, the -ish verb ending and the hope sense.

normal.en: Cherish hides carus, the Latin word for dear, also seen in charity and caress.
normal.cn: cherish 里藏着拉丁语 carus（珍贵的），charity 与 caress 也含这个词根。

normal.en: The -ish ending makes a verb here, as in finish and punish.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ish 词尾构成动词，如 finish 与 punish。

normal.en: You cherish a person, a gift, a memory or a hope; the object is always dear.
normal.cn: cherish 的宾语可以是人、礼物、记忆或希望，共同点是都很珍贵。

normal.en: Cherished is the common adjective: a cherished friend, a cherished habit.
normal.cn: cherished 是常见形容词：珍爱的朋友、珍视的习惯。

normal.en: The past tense cherished doubles no consonant: cherish, cherished.
normal.cn: 过去式 cherished 不双写辅音：cherish 之后直接加 -ed。

abstract.cn: 想象双手把一张褪色照片合在掌心。

abstract.en: Picture a child sleeping with a worn toy under the arm.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子胳膊下夹着一只磨旧的玩具睡去。

abstract.en: Picture a hope kept like a small flame behind cupped hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一点希望像捧在手后的小火苗。

examples.en: They cherished every day they spent together.
examples.cn: 他们珍惜在一起的每一天。

examples.en: He still cherishes the notebook from his first job.
examples.cn: 他仍珍藏着第一份工作时的笔记本。

examples.en: She cherished the hope that the letter would arrive.
examples.cn: 她一直怀着信会寄到的希望。

dict_mnemonic.text: cher 让人想到 cherish 里的「亲爱的」：把心爱之物捧在手心，就是珍爱。

root: 源自拉丁语 carus（珍贵的、亲爱的），经古法语 cher（珍贵）与 cherir（视为珍贵）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Holding something dear gives the sense of loving care, and a dear thing kept close gives the sense of a hope held in the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 把某物视为珍贵给出「爱惜呵护」的意思，而珍贵之物被收在身边又给出「心里怀着」的意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands holding something old and precious.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手捧着一件旧而珍贵的东西。

branches.en: People and objects receive loving care.
branches.cn: 人与物得到充满爱的呵护。

branches.en: Hopes and memories are kept inside.
branches.cn: 希望与记忆被留在心里。

branches.en: The adjective cherished describes what is loved.
branches.cn: 形容词 cherished 描述被爱惜之物。

branches.en: Both senses turn on the value of the object.
branches.cn: 两个义项都围绕对象的价值。

branches.en: A cherished hope can last for years.
branches.cn: 一个被珍藏的希望可以持续多年。

intro.en: Cherish carries the car- root of dearness into a verb.
intro.cn: cherish 把表示「珍贵」的 car- 词根带进动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin carus and caritas stand behind cherish, charity and caress.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carus 与 caritas 是 cherish、charity 与 caress 的共同来源。

items.meaning: loved and valued in the past
items.example: He cherished that summer for years.
She is cherishing her last weeks at home.
items.exampleCN: 她正珍惜在家的最后几周。

items.example: It is a cherished family custom.
items.exampleCN: 这是一个受珍视的家庭习俗。

items.meaning: kindness shown to those in need
items.example: The old word charity shares the same root.

items.meaning: to touch someone gently and lovingly
items.example: She caressed the sleeping child's hair.
items.exampleCN: 她轻抚睡着的孩子的头发。

latinEntries.exampleCN: caritas 给英语提供了 charity。

definition_zh: 非常；极其；糟糕地
definition_en: very, or in a very bad way
core_image: 一桌菜全烧糊了，客人皱着眉
scene: 厨房里飘出一股焦味。 The soup tasted awfully salty.
sceneCN: 这里 awfully 是「非常」（第 2 个义项：口语中表示程度很高）；句意是这汤尝起来咸得厉害。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「糟糕的；可怕的」，awfully 由其加 -ly 构成
由 awful 加 -ness 构成，义为「糟糕；可怕」

senses.title: In a bad way
senses.definition: in a very bad or unpleasant way
senses.definitionCN: 以很糟或令人不快的方式
senses.example: The team played awfully in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队在决赛中打得很糟。
senses.why: Awfully is awful plus -ly, so its literal job is to describe an action done in an awful manner.
senses.whyCN: awfully 是 awful 加 -ly，它本来的职务是描述以糟糕方式完成的动作。

senses.title: Very
senses.definition: used to mean very, especially in polite speech
senses.definitionCN: 表示程度很高，尤用于客气的说法
senses.example: The soup tasted awfully salty.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤尝起来咸得厉害。
senses.why: English speakers often soften strong statements with a word that sounds negative, so awfully drifted into a polite intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 英语使用者常用听起来负面的词来缓和强烈的说法，于是 awfully 漂移成了客气的程度副词。

intro.en: Awfully carries the history of awful into adverb form.
intro.cn: awfully 把 awful 的历史带进了副词形式。

items.en: ege meant 'fear'.
items.cn: ege 意为「恐惧」。

items.en: awe meant fear mixed with wonder.
items.cn: awe 意为恐惧混杂惊叹。

items.en: awful meant 'full of awe'.
items.cn: awful 意为「充满敬畏的」。

items.en: awfully meant 'in a fearful way'.
items.cn: awfully 意为「以可怕的方式」。

items.en: It softened into a polite 'very'.
items.cn: 后来软化为客气的「非常」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aw sound; the near-meaning group gives intensifiers.
note.cn: 形近组都含 aw 音；近义组是表示程度高的词。

entries.definition: very bad or unpleasant
in an embarrassed way
filled with awe
to a high degree
very, or in a bad way
to the greatest degree

normalIntro.en: Awfully works twice: it can describe bad action or simply say very.
normalIntro.cn: awfully 有两种用途：描述糟糕的动作，或单纯表示「非常」。

normal.en: In polite speech awfully usually means very.
normal.cn: 在客气话里 awfully 通常表示「非常」。

normal.en: The adjective is awful, without the -ly.
normal.cn: 形容词是 awful，不带 -ly。

normal.en: Awfully sorry is a common apology.
normal.cn: awfully sorry 是常见的道歉说法。

normal.en: Do not use awfully before a noun.
normal.cn: awfully 不直接修饰名词。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AWE-ful-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: See a burnt dish and a diner's frown.
abstract.cn: 想象烧糊的菜与皱眉的食客。

abstract.en: See a note of apology written in a hurry.
abstract.cn: 想象一张匆匆写下的道歉便条。

abstract.en: See a host bowing a little too low.
abstract.cn: 想象主人微微弯得过低的腰。

examples.en: The team played awfully in the final.
examples.cn: 这支队在决赛中打得很糟。

examples.en: The soup tasted awfully salty.
examples.cn: 这汤尝起来咸得厉害。

examples.en: I am awfully sorry for the delay.
examples.cn: 非常抱歉延误了。

dict_mnemonic.text: awful（糟糕的）加 -ly：本来指做得很糟，口语里却常用来表示「非常」。

root: 由 awful 加 -ly 构成；awful 来自 awe「敬畏」加 -ful「充满」；由「以可怕的方式」弱化为口语中的程度副词「非常」。

sensesIntro.en: The literal bad manner and the polite intensifier are the same word at two temperatures.
sensesIntro.cn: 字面上的「糟糕地」与客气的「非常」，是同一个词的两种温度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a burnt dish and a diner's frown.
core.cn: 核心意象：烧糊的菜与皱眉的食客。

branches.en: played awfully
treated awfully
awfully sorry
awfully kind
awfully tired

intro.en: The -ly suffix turns adjectives into adverbs, as in awfully and quickly.
intro.cn: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词，如 awfully 与 quickly。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the base is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，词基来自日耳曼语。

items.meaning: in an awful way, or very

definition_zh: 任意的；随意的；专断的；武断的
definition_en: based on personal choice rather than reason, or using power without limits
core_image: 裁判随手一指，全凭个人喜好
scene: 规则没有写明，全凭他一句话决定。 The choice of colour seemed arbitrary rather than planned.
sceneCN: 这里 arbitrary 是「随意的」（第 1 个义项：出于个人选择而非理由）；句意是颜色的选择看上去是随手定的，而非事先规划。

derivatives.zh: 副词：任意地；专断地
名词：任意；专断
动词：仲裁，同出 arbiter 一词

senses.title: Chosen at random
senses.definition: decided by personal whim rather than by a rule
senses.definitionCN: 凭个人一时喜好决定，而非依据规则
senses.example: The order of the names on the list is arbitrary.
senses.exampleCN: 名单上名字的排序是随意的。
senses.why: Latin arbitrarius described whatever depended on the will of an arbiter, so the word began as 'left to choice'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 arbitrarius 指「取决于仲裁者意志的」，所以这个词一开始就是「交由选择决定」的意思。

senses.title: Using power without restraint
senses.definition: acting on will alone, with no check from law or others
senses.definitionCN: 只凭意志行事，不受法律或他人约束
senses.example: The ruler made arbitrary arrests without any charge.
senses.exampleCN: 统治者不做任何指控就随意抓人。
senses.why: When the will belongs to a person with power, 'left to choice' turns into 'answerable to nobody', which is the political sense.
senses.whyCN: 当这种意志属于掌权者时，「交由选择」就变成「不受任何人约束」，这就是政治上的专断义。

intro.en: Arbitrary comes from the Latin word for a judge who decides by his own will.
intro.cn: arbitrary 源自拉丁语中表示「凭自己意志裁决的法官」的词。

items.en: arbiter meant 'judge, witness, one who decides'.
items.cn: arbiter 意为「法官、见证人、裁决者」。

items.en: arbitrium meant 'judgment, will, choice'.
items.cn: arbitrium 意为「判断、意志、选择」。

items.en: arbitrarius meant 'depending on the will'.
items.cn: arbitrarius 意为「取决于意志的」。

items.en: English borrowed it for decisions resting on mere will.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，指仅凭意志作出的决定。

items.en: The sense widened from one judge's will to any unchecked power.
items.cn: 词义从一位法官的意志扩展到任何不受制约的权力。

note.en: The look-alike group comes from the same judge root; the near-meaning group gives other words for will without reason.
note.cn: 形近组同出「裁决者」词根；近义组是其他表示无理性凭意志的词。

entries.definition: to settle a dispute
settlement by a judge
a neutral judge
without a plan
changing by whim
ruling by one will

normalIntro.en: Arbitrary means the will decides and nothing else does.
normalIntro.cn: arbitrary 意为只由意志决定，别无其他依据。

normal.en: A judge called an arbiter gave the word its root.
normal.cn: 名为 arbiter 的裁决者给了它词根。

normal.en: Arbitrary rules are the opposite of measured ones.
normal.cn: arbitrary 的规定与有依据的规定相反。

normal.en: The adverb is arbitrarily, often used in complaints.
normal.cn: 副词 arbitrarily 常用于抱怨的语境。

normal.en: Arbitration keeps the same root but means fair judging.
normal.cn: arbitration 同根，却表示公平裁断。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-bi-tra-ry.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-bi-tra-ry。

abstract.en: See a finger pointing at one name without reason.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指毫无理由地点中一个名字。

abstract.en: See a ruler's hand signing without reading.
abstract.cn: 想象掌权者不看内容就签字。

abstract.en: See dice thrown to settle a question.
abstract.cn: 想象掷骰子来决定一个问题。

examples.en: The order of the names on the list is arbitrary.
examples.cn: 名单上名字的排序是随意的。

examples.en: The ruler made arbitrary arrests without any charge.
examples.cn: 统治者不做任何指控就随意抓人。

examples.en: Critics called the deadline arbitrary and unfair.
examples.cn: 批评者称这个期限既武断又不公平。

dict_mnemonic.text: arbiter（裁决者）加 -ary：裁决者想怎么定就怎么定，于是成了随意的、专断的。

root: 来自拉丁语 arbitrarius「取决于意志的」，源自动词 arbiter「裁决者」与 arbitrium「判断、意志」；由「凭裁决者意志」引申出随意与专断两义。

sensesIntro.en: One root covers both a casual choice and a ruler who answers to no one.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词根既涵盖随手的选择，也涵盖不受约束的掌权者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised to point at one option out of many.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在众多选项里随手点向其中一个。

branches.en: an arbitrary choice
arbitrary order
arbitrary power
arbitrary arrests
an arbitrary standard

intro.en: A word about will and judgment that split into fairness and its opposite.
intro.cn: 这个词讲的是意志与判断，后来既生出公正，也生出不公。

latinIntro.en: The root arbiter, 'judge', also gives arbitrate and arbitration.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 arbiter「裁决者」也派生出 arbitrate 与 arbitration。

items.meaning: able to be settled by a judge

definition_zh: 逃跑；逃离；逃避
definition_en: to run away from danger or a place, or to avoid something unpleasant
core_image: 一个人转身冲出门口，连头也不回
scene: 小偷在警察赶到前逃走了。 The thief fled before the police arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 flee 是「逃跑」（第 1 个义项）；句意：小偷在警察赶到前逃走了。

derivatives.zh: 逃跑
逃亡者
逃跑的

senses.title: Run from danger
senses.definition: to run away quickly from danger
senses.definitionCN: 迅速逃离危险
senses.example: The thief fled before the police arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 小偷在警察赶到前逃走了。
senses.why: This is the core sense of physical escape.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体逃离的核心义项。

senses.title: Leave a place
senses.definition: to leave a place quickly because it is unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 因不安全而迅速离开某地
senses.example: Thousands fled the flooded town.
senses.exampleCN: 数千人逃离了被淹的城镇。
senses.why: The danger is a place rather than a pursuer.
senses.whyCN: 危险来自地点而非追捕者。

senses.title: Avoid
senses.definition: to avoid something unpleasant or difficult
senses.definitionCN: 回避令人不快或困难的事物
senses.example: He fled from the question.
senses.exampleCN: 他回避了那个问题。
senses.why: The idea of escape extends from danger to discomfort.
senses.whyCN: 逃离的概念从危险扩展到不适。

intro.en: Flee is a native Germanic verb, Old English fleon, meaning to fly or run away.
intro.cn: flee 是日耳曼语本族动词，古英语 fleon 意为飞走或逃开。

items.en: Fleuhan meant to fly or escape.
items.cn: fleuhan 意为飞走或逃脱。

items.en: Fleon meant to take flight from danger.
items.cn: fleon 意为逃离危险。

items.en: Fleen kept the same sense of running away.
items.cn: fleen 保留了逃跑的意思。

items.en: Flee stayed a strong verb with fled as its past.
items.cn: flee 保持强变化，过去式为 fled。

items.en: The verb also came to mean avoiding a topic.
items.cn: 这个词也引申为回避话题。

note.en: Flee is compared with similar-looking words and with words for escape.
note.cn: 把 flee 与形近词以及表示逃跑的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small jumping insect
the wool of a sheep
a group of ships
to get away from a place
to move fast on foot
to move back or withdraw

normalIntro.en: Flee is flight on foot: the body leaves first and the reason comes later.
normalIntro.cn: flee 是用脚完成的飞走：身体先离开，理由随后才到。

normal.en: They fled the burning house.
normal.cn: 他们逃离了燃烧的房子。

normal.en: The bird fled at our approach.
normal.cn: 鸟在我们靠近时飞走了。

normal.en: He fled from the crowded room.
normal.cn: 他从拥挤的房间逃了出去。

normal.en: Many fled the war.
normal.cn: 许多人逃离了战争。

normal.en: She fled rather than answer.
normal.cn: 她避而不答。

abstract.en: Running away is also a way of deciding.
abstract.cn: 逃跑也是一种做决定的方式。

abstract.en: Some dangers follow the one who flees.
abstract.cn: 有些危险会跟着逃跑的人。

abstract.en: The fastest answer is sometimes distance.
abstract.cn: 有时最快的回答就是拉开距离。

examples.en: The thief fled before the police arrived.
examples.cn: 小偷在警察赶到前逃走了。

examples.en: Thousands fled the flooded town.
examples.cn: 数千人逃离了被淹的城镇。

examples.en: He fled from the question.
examples.cn: 他回避了那个问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: flee 源自古英语 fleon（飞走、逃开），核心义「用最快的速度离开危险」。

root: 源自古英语 fleon（飞走、逃开），与「飞」同族，核心义「迅速离开」。

sensesIntro.en: Flee means to run from danger, to leave an unsafe place, or to avoid something.
sensesIntro.cn: flee 意为逃离危险、离开不安全的地方或回避某事。

core.en: To leave fast because staying is dangerous.
core.cn: 因留下危险而迅速离开。

branches.en: Running from a threat.
Leaving a dangerous place.
Backing away from a hard question.
The threat and the place are often the same.
branches.cn: 威胁与地点常常是同一个。

branches.en: Physical escape becomes emotional escape.
branches.cn: 身体逃离变成情感回避。

intro.en: Flee has a small native family built on flight and escape.
intro.cn: flee 的词族不大，围绕飞行与逃脱构成。

latinIntro.en: Flee has no Latin ancestor; Latin fugere, to flee, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: flee 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 fugere（逃跑）只是语义对应词。

items.example: He flees at the sight of fire.
The fleeing crowd filled the street.
items.exampleCN: 逃跑的人群挤满了街道。

items.example: The refugee found a new home.

items.meaning: a person who has run off

definition_zh: 碳；复写纸
definition_en: a chemical element found in coal, diamonds, and all living things
core_image: 烧成黑色的木炭，仍保留着火的痕迹
scene: 钻石和石墨都由碳构成。 Both diamond and graphite are made of carbon.
sceneCN: 这里 carbon 是「碳」（第 1 个义项：一种化学元素）；句意是钻石和石墨这两种外观完全不同的物质都由碳构成。

derivatives.zh: carbon 加 -ate 构成，义为「碳酸盐」
carbon 加 -ic 构成，义为「碳酸的」
carbon 加 -ize 构成，义为「使碳化」

senses.title: The chemical element of coal and diamonds
senses.definition: a chemical element that forms coal, diamonds, and the bodies of living things
senses.definitionCN: 构成煤、钻石和生物体的一种化学元素
senses.example: Carbon is the basic building block of all living things.
senses.exampleCN: 碳是一切生物的基本组成单元。
senses.why: Latin carbo meant charcoal or a glowing coal, the visible form of this element.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 carbo 指木炭或烧红的炭，正是这种元素最直观的形态。

senses.title: Thin paper that copies writing
senses.definition: thin dark paper placed under a sheet so that writing passes through
senses.definitionCN: 垫在纸下、让字迹透过去的深色薄纸
senses.example: The receipt was typed with carbon paper.
senses.exampleCN: 那张收据是用复写纸打出来的。
senses.why: The black coating on such paper is made of carbon, so the paper took the element's name.
senses.whyCN: 这种纸上的黑色涂层由碳制成，于是纸张直接借用了元素的名字。

intro.en: Carbon is an old charcoal word that chemistry gave a precise new meaning.
intro.cn: carbon 是一个古老的「木炭」词，化学给了它精确的新含义。

items.en: carbo meant a piece of charcoal or a glowing coal.
items.cn: carbo 指一块木炭或烧红的炭。

items.en: French chemists used carbone for the element they had isolated from charcoal.
items.cn: 法国化学家用 carbone 称呼他们从木炭中分离出的元素。

items.en: English borrowed carbone as carbon during the chemical revolution.
items.cn: 在化学革命期间，英语借入 carbone，写作 carbon。

items.en: The word spread into compounds such as carbon dioxide and carbon paper.
items.cn: 这个词扩散到二氧化碳、复写纸等复合词中。

items.en: Today carbon is central to climate talk, as in carbon footprint and carbon emissions.
items.cn: 今天 carbon 是气候话题的核心词，如碳足迹与碳排放。

note.en: Carbon has a large chemical family, and it is also the name of several very different materials.
note.cn: carbon 有一个庞大的化学词族，同时也指几种外观差别很大的材料。

entries.definition: a salt containing carbon and oxygen
entries.definitionCN: 含碳和氧的盐类，由 carbon 加 -ate 构成。

entries.definition: relating to carbon, especially in acids
entries.definitionCN: 与碳有关的，尤指碳酸的。

entries.definition: to turn something into carbon or charcoal
black material made by burning wood slowly
entries.definitionCN: 木材慢烧制成的黑色材料，与 carbon 的古义最接近。

entries.definition: a soft black form of carbon used in pencils
entries.definitionCN: 石墨，一种柔软的黑色碳单质，用于铅笔芯。

entries.definition: a very hard clear form of carbon
entries.definitionCN: 钻石，碳的一种极硬透明形态。

normalIntro.en: The element hides inside the old word for charcoal, and the family shows its many forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这个元素躲在古老的「木炭」词里，而词族展示了它的多种形态。

normal.en: carbon comes from Latin carbo, charcoal, so the word is older than chemistry.
normal.cn: carbon 来自拉丁语 carbo（木炭），这个词比化学更古老。

normal.en: carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide name gases built on carbon.
normal.cn: carbon dioxide 与 carbon monoxide 都是以碳为基础的气体名称。

normal.en: carbon paper copies writing because its black layer is carbon.
normal.cn: 复写纸能复印字迹，是因为它的黑色涂层就是碳。

normal.en: carbon footprint measures the carbon a person or product leaves behind.
normal.cn: 碳足迹衡量一个人或一件产品留下的碳排放。

normal.en: Carbon is uncountable, so it takes no plural in ordinary use.
normal.cn: carbon 作元素名时不可数，日常使用没有复数。

abstract.en: Picture a blackened stick pulled from a fire, still warm.
abstract.cn: 想象一根从火里抽出的黑木棍，还带着余温。

abstract.en: Picture the same element as dull pencil lead and as a brilliant diamond.
abstract.cn: 想象同一种元素，一面是暗灰的铅笔芯，一面是璀璨的钻石。

abstract.en: Picture a dark layer under a sheet of paper catching every stroke of the pen.
abstract.cn: 想象纸下那层黑色材料，接住笔尖的每一次划动。

examples.en: Both diamond and graphite are made of carbon.
examples.cn: 钻石和石墨都由碳构成。

examples.en: Carbon is the basic building block of all living things.
examples.cn: 碳是一切生物的基本组成单元。

examples.en: The receipt was typed with carbon paper.
examples.cn: 那张收据是用复写纸打出来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡本」——烧成炭的木本，剩下的黑色就是碳。

root: 拉丁语 carbo（木炭、炭火）→ 法语 carbone → 英语 carbon；同根词有 charcoal、carbonic。

sensesIntro.en: One element appears as charcoal, as diamond, and as the black layer of copying paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种元素，既以木炭出现，也以钻石出现，还以复写纸的黑色涂层出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: black charcoal left after fire, the visible trace of one element.
core.cn: 核心意象：火熄灭后留下的黑炭，是一种元素可见的痕迹。

branches.en: The chemical sense: the element shared by coal, diamonds, and living tissue.
branches.cn: 化学义：煤、钻石与生物组织共有的元素。

branches.en: The office sense: dark paper that transfers writing.
branches.cn: 办公义：能转印字迹的深色纸张。

branches.en: Compounds such as carbon dioxide and carbon fibre are built on the element.
branches.cn: 二氧化碳、碳纤维等复合词都以这一元素为基础。

branches.en: Climate language turns the element into a measure of human impact.
branches.cn: 气候话题把这一元素变成了衡量人类影响的指标。

branches.en: The copying sense survives mainly in carbon paper and carbon copy.
branches.cn: 复写义主要保留在复写纸与副本这两个说法里。

intro.en: Carbon is a base noun from Latin, and chemistry built a large family on it.
intro.cn: carbon 是来自拉丁语的基础名词，化学在它之上建起了一个大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin carbo, charcoal, is the source of carbon and of several chemical terms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carbo（木炭）是 carbon 及若干化学术语的来源。

items.meaning: the element found in coal and diamonds
items.meaningCN: 碳，存在于煤和钻石中的元素
items.example: Carbon has six protons in each atom.
items.exampleCN: 每个碳原子有六个质子。

items.example: The rock is mostly calcium carbonate.
items.exampleCN: 这块岩石主要是碳酸钙。

items.example: Carbonic acid forms when gas dissolves in water.
items.exampleCN: 气体溶于水时形成碳酸。

items.example: The heat carbonized the outer layer of wood.

items.meaningCN: 含二氧化碳的，指碳酸饮料

items.example: The city plans to decarbonize its buses.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市计划让公交车脱碳。

items.meaning: black material made by burning wood

definition_zh: 便携的；可携带的；轻便的；可移植的；便携设备
definition_en: light and small enough to be carried easily, designed for use in different places, able to be moved to another system or job, or a small device that can be carried
core_image: 一台合上盖子就能塞进背包的笔记本电脑，提手上还留着体温
scene: 清晨的候车室里，一名记者把折叠好的小键盘从背包里取出来，放在膝上。 She carries a portable keyboard so she can write on the train.
sceneCN: 这里 portable 是「便携的」（第 1 个义项：轻便、容易携带）；句意为她带着一个便携键盘，好在火车上写作。图中可辨识物件：候车室、背包、小键盘。

pos.zh: 便携的；可携带的；轻便的；可移植的

derivatives.zh: 由 portable 加 -ity 构成，义为「便携性；可移植性」
由 portable 加 -ly 构成，义为「便携地；可携带地」
由 trans-（穿过）加拉丁 portare（搬运）与 -able 构成，与 portable 共享词根，义为「可运输的」

senses.title: Light enough to be carried
senses.definition: small and light enough that a person can carry it from place to place without difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 体积与重量都小，一个人可以毫不费力地带着它到处走
senses.example: The radio is small and portable enough to fit in a coat pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 这台收音机很小，便携得能放进大衣口袋。
senses.why: Latin portare means to carry and -abilis means able to be, so the adjective starts as a plain claim that an object can be carried.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 portare 意为搬运，-abilis 意为「能够被……」；这个形容词起初只是直说一件东西可以被带着走。

senses.title: Designed to be used on the move
senses.definition: of equipment, built to work in different places rather than fixed in one room or building
senses.definitionCN: 指设备被造得可以在不同地点使用，而不是固定在一间屋子或一栋楼里
senses.example: The clinic uses a portable X-ray machine for home visits.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所用一台便携式 X 光机出诊。
senses.why: Once a machine can be carried, it can also be used where the patient is; the sense shifts from the weight of the object to the freedom of the place it can serve.
senses.whyCN: 一台机器只要能搬动，就能到病人所在的地方使用；义项于是从物体的重量转到它能服务的地点自由。

senses.title: Able to be moved to another system
senses.definition: of software, skills or benefits, able to be moved from one computer system, employer or country to another
senses.definitionCN: 指软件、技能或福利能够从一套计算机系统、一个雇主或一个国家转移到另一个
senses.example: The pension is portable, so workers keep it when they change jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 这份养老金可以转移，所以工人换工作时能把它带走。
senses.why: The carrying image is applied to things that are not physical: a skill or a pension is portable if it travels with the person instead of staying behind.
senses.whyCN: 「搬运」的形象被用到非实物上：一项技能或一份养老金若能跟着人走而不是留在原处，就是 portable。

senses.title: A small device that can be carried
senses.definition: a small machine such as a radio, television or computer that is designed to be carried around
senses.definitionCN: 收音机、电视或电脑之类为随身携带而设计的小型机器
senses.example: He listened to the match on a little portable in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 他在厨房用一台小便携收音机听比赛。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun when the object is obvious from context; the portable is simply the portable set.
senses.whyCN: 当所指物品在语境里已经很明显，英语常把形容词直接当名词用；the portable 就是「那台便携的机器」。

intro.en: Portable is Latin portare, to carry, plus the suffix -abilis, able to be; it reached English through Old French as a plain adjective for things easy to move.
intro.cn: portable 是拉丁语 portare（搬运）加上后缀 -abilis（能够被……）构成的，经古法语进入英语，最初只是形容容易搬动的东西。

items.en: Portare is the Latin verb for carrying, and it also stands behind porter, transport and import.
items.cn: portare 是拉丁语中表示搬运的动词，porter、transport、import 也都出自它。

items.en: The suffix -abilis marked what can be done to something, as in the modern English -able.
items.cn: 后缀 -abilis 表示「可以被……的」，相当于现代英语的 -able。

items.en: Portabilis joined the two: an object that can be carried, with no suggestion yet of electronics or jobs.
items.cn: portabilis 把两者合起来，指可以被携带的物体，那时还没有电子产品或职业的含义。

items.en: Old French kept the adjective as portable, and English borrowed it in the late Middle Ages for furniture and small goods that could be moved.
items.cn: 古法语保留了这个形容词 portable，英语在中世纪后期借入，用来形容可以搬动的家具与小件物品。

items.en: Modern English applies it to radios, computers, pensions and software, so the word now measures how easily something travels with its owner.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用在收音机、电脑、养老金与软件上，于是这个词衡量的是某物能多方便地跟着主人走。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers family forms and the harbor word port; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for things easy to move or hold.
note.cn: 形近组收同族形式以及表示港口的 port；近义组收形容容易移动或持握之物的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being easy to carry or move to another system.
entries.definitionCN: 由 portable 加 -ity 构成，义为「便携性；可移植性」。

entries.definition: A harbor or an opening for a cable; this word comes from Latin portus, not from portare.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，但表示港口的 port 来自拉丁 portus，与 portable 的搬运词根不同。

entries.definition: A person who carries luggage, built on the same Latin verb portare.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一拉丁动词 portare 构成，指替人搬运行李的人。

entries.definition: Able to be transported; the same carrying verb with the prefix trans-.
entries.definitionCN: 由 trans-（穿过）加同一搬运词根与 -able 构成，义为「可运输的」。

entries.definition: Able to move or be moved easily.
entries.definitionCN: 可移动的；强调能移动，不强调能随身携带。

entries.definition: Small and neatly fitted into little space.
entries.definitionCN: 紧凑的；强调体积小、占空间少。

entries.definition: Small enough to be held and used in the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 手持的；强调用手握住使用。

entries.definition: Weighing less than usual and therefore easy to move.

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin verb for carrying plus a suffix of possibility, and its family keeps returning to light objects that travel with their owner.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「搬运」动词加上表示可能性的后缀，同族词反复回到能跟着主人走动的轻便物件。

normal.en: Portable is portare plus -abilis, so its oldest meaning is simply able to be carried.
normal.cn: portable 是 portare 加 -abilis，所以它最古老的意思就是「可以被搬运的」。

normal.en: Porter takes the same verb and adds -er for the person; portable describes the thing, porter the one who carries it.
normal.cn: porter 用同一个动词加 -er 指人；portable 形容东西，porter 指搬东西的人。

normal.en: Portability adds -ity to portable and names the quality, which is why portable software can run on more than one system.
normal.cn: portability 在 portable 后加 -ity，指这种性质，所以 portable software 能在不止一套系统上运行。

normal.en: A portable pension or a portable skill travels with the worker instead of staying with one employer.
normal.cn: 可转移的养老金或可迁移的技能会跟着工人走，而不是留在某一位雇主那里。

normal.en: Transportable adds trans-, across, to the same carrying root, so it means able to be carried from place to place.
normal.cn: transportable 在同一搬运词根前加 trans-（穿过），意为可以从一处运到另一处。

abstract.en: Portable things are not merely light; their usefulness travels with them.
abstract.cn: 便携之物不只是轻，它们的好处能跟着人一起移动。

abstract.en: A skill is portable when no single employer owns it, which is why the word moved from radios to careers.
abstract.cn: 一项技能若不属于某一位雇主，就是可转移的；这也解释了这个词为何从收音机走到了职业。

abstract.en: Anything portable asks for a smaller form, not a smaller purpose.
abstract.cn: 任何便携之物要求的是更小的形体，而不是更小的用途。

examples.en: She carries a portable keyboard so she can write on the train.
examples.cn: 她带着一个便携键盘，好在火车上写作。

examples.en: The pension is portable, so workers keep it when they change jobs.
examples.cn: 这份养老金可以转移，所以工人换工作时能把它带走。

examples.en: The clinic uses a portable X-ray machine for home visits.
examples.cn: 这家诊所用一台便携式 X 光机出诊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡特薄」——薄薄一台，提起来就能走；portable 就是便携的、可携带的。

root: 由拉丁 portare（搬运）加 -abilis（能……的）构成，经古法语 portable 进入英语；与 porter（搬运工）、transport（运输）同出一源。注意与来自 portus（港口）的 port 区分：拼写相近，拉丁来源不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an object that can be carried; the senses divide into its lightness, its use on the move, its transfer to other systems, and the device itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是可以被带着走的物件；义项由此分出轻便、可在移动中使用、可转移到别的系统，以及这种设备本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a laptop closing into a backpack, its handle still warm from the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台合上盖子就能塞进背包的笔记本电脑，提手上还留着体温。

branches.en: a radio slipping into a coat pocket
an X-ray machine wheeled into a patient's home
branches.cn: X 光机被推进病人家中

branches.en: a pension account moving to a new employer
branches.cn: 养老金账户转到新雇主名下

branches.en: a small radio playing on a kitchen shelf
branches.cn: 厨房搁板上响着的小收音机

branches.en: skills that travel with a worker from job to job
branches.cn: 随工人换工作而迁移的技能

intro.en: The adjective is built from the Latin verb for carrying and a suffix of possibility, and the same pieces also build porter, portability and transportable.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由拉丁语「搬运」动词与表示可能性的后缀构成，同样的部件还造出了 porter、portability 与 transportable。

latinIntro.en: Portable goes back to the Latin verb portare, to carry, and the adjective portabilis, able to be carried; the family is Latin rather than Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: portable 上溯拉丁动词 portare（搬运）与形容词 portabilis（可携带的）；这个词族属于拉丁语而非日耳曼语。

items.meaning: able to be carried or moved

definition_zh: 逐步的；渐进的；进步的；主张改革的；（语法）进行体的；（税）累进的；改革派人士
definition_en: moving forward in stages, favouring social reform, or naming a verb form that shows an action still in progress
core_image: 沿着台阶一级一级向上走，每一脚都踩在上一级上
scene: 这套课程的难度会随进度逐步提高。 Public health officials described the outbreak as a progressive disease that worsens over months rather than days.
sceneCN: 这里 progressive 是「逐阶段加重的」（第 3 个义项：病情按阶段持续恶化）；句意：公共卫生官员称这次暴发是一种在数月而非数日里逐步加重的疾病。图中可辨识物件：一张张翻过的日历、由浅入深的病情曲线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 渐进的；进步的；主张改革的；进行体的；累进的
改革派人士；（语法）进行体形式

derivatives.zh: 进步；前进；推进
渐进；一系列步骤；序列
逐渐地；越来越多地
后退的；退步的；逆向的

senses.title: Moving ahead in stages
senses.definition: describing change that takes place step by step rather than all at once
senses.definitionCN: 指变化不是一次性完成，而是分阶段一步一步发生的
senses.example: The textbook offers a progressive introduction to statistics, one chapter at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这本教材一章一节地逐步介绍统计学。
senses.why: Pro- means 'forward' and gradi means 'to step', so progredi was 'to walk forward'. The suffix -ive turns that walk into an adjective for anything that keeps stepping ahead.
senses.whyCN: pro- 意为“向前”，gradi 意为“迈步”，因此 progredi 就是“向前走”。后缀 -ive 把这次行走变成形容词，用来形容任何不断向前迈步的事物。

senses.title: Favouring social reform
senses.definition: supporting changes in law, education or the economy in order to improve society
senses.definitionCN: 支持在法律、教育或经济方面作出改变，以求改善社会
senses.example: The mayor ran on a progressive platform of housing and transit reform.
senses.exampleCN: 这位市长以住房与交通改革的进步纲领参加竞选。
senses.why: Around 1900 the forward-step image was applied to politics: people who wanted society to move ahead began to call themselves progressive.
senses.whyCN: 大约在 1900 年，向前迈步的意象被用到政治上：希望社会向前走的人开始自称 progressive。

senses.title: Growing worse stage by stage
senses.definition: of an illness: continuing to develop and worsen over time in stages
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病随时间分阶段持续发展、逐渐加重
senses.example: Doctors warned that the progressive loss of hearing could not be reversed.
senses.exampleCN: 医生警告说，这种逐步加重的听力丧失无法逆转。
senses.why: Medical usage keeps only the stepping part of the image. The illness keeps advancing step after step, and the direction happens to be bad.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法只保留了意象中“迈步”的部分：疾病一步一步向前推进，只是方向恰好是不好的那一边。

senses.title: Grammar: action still running
senses.definition: the verb form that presents an action as ongoing at a stated moment
senses.definitionCN: 指把动作呈现为在某一时刻仍在持续进行的动词形式
senses.example: English marks ongoing action with the progressive form, as in 'he is reading'.
senses.exampleCN: 英语用进行体标记正在持续的动作，例如“他正在阅读”。
senses.why: The action is pictured mid-stride, caught while it is still walking. Grammarians named the be + -ing form after that unfinished step.
senses.whyCN: 动作被画在半路上，正是在它还在走的时候被抓住。语法学家就用这个未完成的步子来命名 be + -ing 形式。

senses.title: Tax rates that climb with income
senses.definition: of a tax: taking a larger share from higher bands of income
senses.definitionCN: 指对更高收入档次征收更大比例的税
senses.example: Under a progressive income tax, higher earners pay a larger share of their income.
senses.exampleCN: 在累进所得税制下，收入更高的人按其收入缴纳更大比例。
senses.why: Each income band steps up to a higher rate, so the tax ladder rises as the figure rises: the staircase image moved into numbers.
senses.whyCN: 每一收入档次都向上迈到更高的税率，税级随收入上升而上升：台阶的意象被搬进了数字里。

senses.title: Ahead of current thinking
senses.definition: modern in outlook, especially in education, art or social policy
senses.definitionCN: 指在教育、艺术或社会政策上观念现代、走在前面
senses.example: Her progressive views on assessment upset the traditional examiners.
senses.exampleCN: 她在评估方式上的进步观点让传统考官感到不安。
senses.why: Here the forward step measures ideas against the present: whatever stands ahead of current practice is called progressive.
senses.whyCN: 这里向前的一步是用当下衡量观念：凡站在现行做法之前的，就被称为 progressive。

senses.title: A supporter of reform
senses.definition: a person who belongs to or supports a reformist political group
senses.definitionCN: 指属于或支持改革派政治团体的人
senses.example: The committee split between progressives and conservatives over the zoning plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在分区规划上分裂为改革派与保守派。
senses.why: The political adjective was turned into a countable noun in the early 20th century, first in American party language.
senses.whyCN: 这个政治形容词在 20 世纪初被转为可数名词，最早出现在美国政党用语中。

senses.title: The progressive form itself
senses.definition: the grammatical form or construction that expresses ongoing action
senses.definitionCN: 指表达持续动作的语法形式或结构
senses.example: 'Is eating' is a progressive, while 'eats' is a simple present.
senses.exampleCN: “is eating”是进行体，而“eats”是一般现在时。
senses.why: In grammar books the adjective became a countable noun naming the form; the term is short for 'progressive tense' or 'progressive aspect'.
senses.whyCN: 在语法书里，这个形容词变成可数名词来指形式；这个说法是“进行时态”或“进行体”的简称。

intro.en: Progressive joins pro-, 'forward', with gradi, 'to step', and then adds the adjective suffix -ive. The Latin verb progredi meant 'to walk forward', and its participle progressus gave the noun progress. The adjective simply describes whatever keeps stepping ahead, whether a disease, a tax scale, a verb form or a political programme.
intro.cn: progressive 由 pro-“向前”、gradi“迈步”与形容词后缀 -ive 组成。拉丁动词 progredi 意为“向前走”，其分词 progressus 产生了名词 progress。这个形容词只是描述任何不断向前迈步的事物——无论是一种疾病、一张税率表、一个动词形式，还是一套政治纲领。

items.en: The root behind Latin gradi, 'to step', is reconstructed as *ghredh-. It is generally believed to be the source of the Latin words for step and grade.
items.cn: 拉丁 gradi“迈步”背后的词根被重构为 *ghredh-，一般认为它是拉丁语中表示“步、等级”的一组词的来源。

items.en: Gradi was a deponent verb meaning 'to walk, to step'. Its noun partner gradus meant 'a step' and also 'a rank or degree', and both feed the modern word family.
items.cn: gradi 是异态动词，意为“走、迈步”。其名词伙伴 gradus 表示“一步”，也表示“等级、程度”，两者都滋养了现代词族。

items.en: The prefix added direction: progredi meant 'to step forward', and its past participle progressus became the noun for forward movement.
items.cn: 前缀赋予方向：progredi 意为“向前迈步”，其过去分词 progressus 成为表示“前进”的名词。

items.en: French progressif and Medieval Latin progressivus gave English progressive. Early uses were physical: a progressive motion, a progressive disease.
items.cn: 法语 progressif 与中古拉丁 progressivus 给英语带来了 progressive。早期用法是物理性的：向前运动、进行性疾病。

items.en: Reform politics borrowed the forward image: a progressive wanted society to move ahead. Progressive taxation, with rates rising band by band, uses the same staircase in numbers.
items.cn: 改革政治借用了向前的意象：progressive 想让社会向前走。累进税制让税率逐档上升，把同一座台阶搬进了数字里。

items.en: Grammarians named the be + -ing form the progressive because it presents an action caught in the middle of happening, not finished.
items.cn: 语法学家把 be + -ing 形式命名为进行体，因为它呈现的是发生在半途、尚未结束的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the noun progress, the abstract progression, the adverb and the opposite-prefix regressive. The meaning group contrasts kinds of forward movement and kinds of reform.
note.cn: 形近组区分名词 progress、抽象名词 progression、副词形式与反向前缀的 regressive；词义组比较不同类型的向前推进与不同类型的改革主张。

entries.definition: forward movement or improvement; to move forward. It names the movement itself, while progressive describes something that has that character.
entries.definitionCN: 向前运动或改进；向前推进。它命名运动本身，而 progressive 描述具备这种性质的事物。

entries.definition: a series of steps or stages in order. It stresses sequence, while progressive stresses the direction of travel.
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序排列的一系列步骤或阶段。它强调次序，而 progressive 强调行进方向。

entries.definition: in stages, or increasingly. It turns the adjective into a statement about how something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 分阶段地，或越来越……地。它把形容词转为对发生方式的陈述。

entries.definition: moving backward, especially undoing reform. It is built on the same Latin step but with re- 'back' instead of pro- 'forward'.
entries.definitionCN: 向后退的，尤指取消改革。它建立在同一个拉丁“步”词根上，只是用 re-“向后”取代了 pro-“向前”。

entries.definition: far along in development. It says where something stands, not that it moves in stages.
entries.definitionCN: 发展程度高的。它说明某物所处的位置，而不表示它分阶段推进。

entries.definition: happening slowly by small degrees. It shares the step image but carries no political or grammatical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 以微小程度缓慢发生的。它共享台阶意象，但不含政治或语法含义。

entries.definition: going on without a break. It stresses an unbroken span, while progressive stresses a series of advancing stages.
entries.definitionCN: 不中断地持续。它强调连续不断，而 progressive 强调一连串前进的阶段。

entries.definition: favouring gradual change in institutions. It is close to senses 02 and 07 but names the doctrine rather than the forward image.
entries.definitionCN: 主张对制度作渐进改革的。它接近第 2 与第 7 义项，但命名的是主张，而非向前的意象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word as pro + grad + ive, then let the staircase cover stages, illness, tax bands, grammar and politics.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 pro + grad + ive，再用台阶意象串起阶段、病情、税档、语法与政治。

normal.en: Split it into pro + gress + ive: forward, step, adjective. The word literally means 'stepping forward'.
normal.cn: 拆成 pro + gress + ive：向前、迈步、形容词。这个词字面就是“向前迈步的”。

normal.en: Picture a staircase: every step stands on the one below, so nothing jumps to the top.
normal.cn: 想象一座楼梯：每一级都踩在下一级上，没有哪一步能跳到顶端。

normal.en: A progressive disease climbs the same stairs, only downward in terms of health.
normal.cn: 进行性疾病爬的是同一座楼梯，只是在健康上朝下走。

normal.en: In a progressive tax, each income band sits one stair higher than the last.
normal.cn: 在累进税中，每一收入档次都比上一档高一级台阶。

normal.en: A progressive in politics is someone who wants the whole society to take the next step.
normal.cn: 政治上的改革派，就是希望整个社会迈出下一步的人。

abstract.en: Think of time as a ladder rather than a line: 'progressive' always implies rungs, never a smooth slope.
abstract.cn: 把时间想成梯子而不是直线：progressive 总暗示横档，而不是平滑斜坡。

abstract.en: Notice that the medical sense keeps the motion but drops the hope: stepping forward can also mean going further into illness.
abstract.cn: 注意医学义保留了运动却丢掉了希望：向前迈步也可能意味着更深地陷入疾病。

abstract.en: Hold present and progressive apart: one stands still at a point in time, the other is photographed mid-stride.
abstract.cn: 把“现在”与“进行”分开：一个静止在时间点上，另一个被拍在迈步的半途。

examples.en: The school adopted a progressive curriculum that adds one skill level at a time.
examples.cn: 这所学校采用了逐级增加技能的渐进式课程。

examples.en: Specialists tracked the progressive weakening of the patient's muscles.
examples.cn: 专家追踪了病人肌肉逐步变弱的过程。

examples.en: Economists debated whether a progressive tax on vacant land would cool the market.
examples.cn: 经济学家争论对闲置土地征收累进税是否能给市场降温。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“扑罗格瑞斯”：一步一扑向前走，越走越进步。

root: 拉丁 progredi“向前走”（pro- 向前 + gradi 迈步），过去分词 progressus，加 -ive 构成形容词；核心意象是“一级一级往前走”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep someone or something walking forward. A course moves through levels, an illness moves through stages, a tax scale moves through bands, a verb form catches an action mid-stride, a reformer wants society to take the next step, and grammar turns the adjective into a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留了“有人在向前走”：课程逐级推进，疾病逐段发展，税率逐档上升，动词形式把动作抓在半途，改革者希望社会迈出下一步，语法则把这个形容词变成名词。

core.en: Stepping forward, one stage at a time, until the new position stands ahead of the old one.
core.cn: 一步一步向前，每迈一步都进入新阶段，直到新的位置站在旧位置之前。

branches.en: STAGES: change arrives one step at a time, whether it improves health or worsens it.
branches.cn: 阶段：变化一步一步到来，无论它让健康变好还是变坏。

branches.en: POLITICS: the forward step becomes a demand for reform and a name for its supporters.
branches.cn: 政治：向前的一步变成改革诉求，也成为支持者的名称。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the action is shown mid-step, and the form itself takes the adjective as a name.
branches.cn: 语法：动作被展示在半步之中，形式本身也借用了这个形容词作名称。

branches.en: NUMBERS: the staircase becomes tax bands that climb with income.
branches.cn: 数字：台阶变成随收入上升的税档。

branches.en: OUTLOOK: ideas are ranked by how far ahead of present practice they stand.
branches.cn: 观念：思想按它们领先当下做法的程度来排序。

intro.en: Progressive stacks pro-, the verb gradi and the adjective suffix -ive. The items below show the same base with other endings, and the opposite prefix re- building the reverse idea.
intro.cn: progressive 叠加了 pro-、动词 gradi 与形容词后缀 -ive。下列条目展示同一词基配其他词尾，以及反向前缀 re- 构成的相反概念。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb, its noun and its participle. They explain why one word family covers walking, ranking, taxation and grammar.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出动词、名词与分词，解释了为什么同一词族能覆盖行走、等级、征税与语法。

items.meaning: moving forward in stages; favouring reform
items.meaningCN: 分阶段向前的；主张改革的
items.example: The reform was introduced in progressive stages.
The report noted steady progress in literacy.
items.exampleCN: 报告指出识字率稳步提高。

items.example: The progression from trainee to supervisor takes years.
items.exampleCN: 从实习生到主管的晋升需要数年。

items.example: The light faded progressively after sunset.
items.exampleCN: 日落之后光线逐渐变暗。

items.meaning: the quality of favouring advance or reform
items.example: Critics questioned the progressiveness of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 批评者质疑该方案的进步性。

items.example: The new fee was criticized as a regressive measure.
items.exampleCN: 这项新收费被批评为倒退措施。

items.example: The paint comes in fine gradations of grey.
items.exampleCN: 这种颜料有细致的灰色层次。
康复虽然缓慢，但很彻底。

definition_zh: 声音的，音频的；音频，声音信号
definition_en: relating to sound that is recorded or broadcast, or the recorded sound itself
core_image: 一排跳动的波形，把看不见的声音画成看得见的线
scene: 剪辑师把画面定住，先单独处理声音那条轨道。 The audio was clearer than the video.
sceneCN: 这里 audio 是「音频、声音信号」（第 2 个义项）；句意是音频比画面清楚。

derivatives.zh: 名词：有声书
形容词：视听的
名词：音响发烧友

senses.title: Relating to sound
senses.definition: connected with sound that is recorded, played back or broadcast
senses.definitionCN: 与录制、播放或播出的声音有关的
senses.example: The audio cable was loose at the back.
senses.exampleCN: 音频线在后面松了。
senses.why: As an adjective it simply labels the sound side of any system, standing opposite video in the same sentence.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，它只是给任何系统里「声音那一侧」贴标签，在同一句里与 video 相对。

senses.title: The sound itself
senses.definition: the recorded or transmitted sound itself
senses.definitionCN: 被录制或传输的声音本身
senses.example: The audio was clearer than the video.
senses.exampleCN: 音频比画面清楚。
senses.why: As a noun it turns the adjective into a mass of data: not a sound in the air, but a signal stored in a file.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，形容词变成了可供处理的一团数据：不是空气里的声音，而是存在文件里的信号。

intro.en: Audio is simply the Latin word for 'I hear', taken whole into modern technology.
intro.cn: audio 就是拉丁语「我听见」，被整体搬进了现代技术。

items.en: audire meant 'to hear'.
items.cn: audire 意为「听见」。

items.en: audio was the first person form, 'I hear'.
items.cn: audio 是第一人称形式，意为「我听见」。

items.en: The root aud- was used to name hearing and sound.
items.cn: 词根 aud- 被用来命名听觉与声音。

items.en: audio labeled the sound channel beside video.
items.cn: 录音时代用 audio 标注与视频并列的声音通道。

items.en: It now covers files, streams and equipment.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖文件、流媒体与设备。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aud- root; the near-meaning group gives other words for sound.
note.cn: 形近组共享 aud- 词根；近义组是其他表示声音的词。

a trial performance
able to be heard

normalIntro.en: Audio marks the sound half of any media system.
normalIntro.cn: audio 标注的是任何媒体系统里「声音的那一半」。

normal.en: The root aud- means hear, the same one in audience.
normal.cn: 词根 aud- 意为「听」，与 audience 同源。

normal.en: Audio is the everyday partner of video.
normal.cn: audio 是 video 最日常的搭档。

normal.en: It stays the same in the plural, and usually takes no article as a noun.
normal.cn: 它复数形式不变，作名词时通常不加冠词。

normal.en: An audio file is a file that holds sound.
normal.cn: audio file 就是存放声音的文件。

normal.en: Audiobook simply joins audio and book.
normal.cn: audiobook 就是把 audio 与 book 拼在一起。

abstract.en: See a waveform rising and falling on a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一条上下起伏的波形。

abstract.en: See two cables, one for sound and one for picture.
abstract.cn: 想象两根线，一根走声音，一根走画面。

abstract.en: See a pair of headphones resting on a script.
abstract.cn: 想象一副耳机搁在剧本上。

examples.en: The audio was clearer than the video.
examples.cn: 音频比画面清楚。

examples.en: The audio cable was loose at the back.
examples.cn: 音频线在后面松了。

examples.en: She listened to the audio while reading the notes.
examples.cn: 她一边看笔记一边听录音。

dict_mnemonic.text: audi（听）加 -o：凡是被听见、被录下来的声音都归它管，所以音频文件、音频线、音质都用 audio。

root: 直接借自拉丁语 audio「我听见」，词根 audire 意为「听」；二十世纪录音与广播技术把它固定为「声音信号」的标签，与 video 相对。

sensesIntro.en: The same word labels the sound channel and the sound data inside it.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既标注声音通道，也指通道里流动的声音数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a waveform drawn as a line of hills and valleys.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条画成山峰与山谷的波形线。

intro.en: The root aud-, 'to hear', runs through audio, audience and audition.
intro.cn: 词根 aud- 意为「听」，贯穿 audio、audience 与 audition。

latinIntro.en: Latin audire, 'to hear', also gives audible and inaudible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 audire「听见」也是 audible 与 inaudible 的来源。

definition_zh: 马克杯；大杯子；一杯的量；脸；抢劫
definition_en: a large cup with a handle, the amount it holds, an informal word for a face, and a verb meaning to rob someone, especially in the street
core_image: 一只厚壁带柄的大杯，杯口冒着热气
scene: 清晨的厨房里水壶刚响，桌上还摆着昨晚没洗的杯子。 He poured steaming tea into a thick ceramic mug.
sceneCN: 这里是「马克杯、大杯子」（第 1 个义项：带柄的大杯）；句意为他往厚实的陶瓷杯里倒热茶。图中可辨识物件：水壶、马克杯、厨房台面。

pos.zh: 马克杯；大杯子；一杯的量；脸

derivatives.zh: 由 mug 加 -er 构成，义为「抢劫者」
由 mug 加 -ing 构成，义为「街头抢劫」
由 mug 加 -ful 构成，义为「一杯的量」

senses.title: A large drinking cup with a handle
senses.definition: a large, often cylindrical cup with a handle, used for hot drinks
senses.definitionCN: 带柄的大杯，通常呈圆筒状，用来盛热饮
senses.example: She filled a thick ceramic mug with hot tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她往一只厚实的陶瓷杯里倒满热茶。
senses.why: The word first named a drinking vessel in sixteenth-century English, and that solid object is still the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词十六世纪在英语里先指一种饮器，那个实实在在的物件至今仍是核心义项。

senses.title: The amount a mug holds
senses.definition: the quantity of liquid that fits in such a cup
senses.definitionCN: 这样一只杯子所能容纳的液体量
senses.example: He drank a whole mug of milk before the run.
senses.exampleCN: 跑步前他喝了一整杯牛奶。
senses.why: A container can stand for its contents, so the cup easily becomes a unit of measure for what is poured into it.
senses.whyCN: 容器可以代指所装的东西，于是杯子很自然地变成衡量倒入其中之物的一单位。

senses.title: A face, informally
senses.definition: a person's face, used informally and often with a hint of roughness
senses.definitionCN: 人的脸，属非正式用法，常带一点粗鲁的意味
senses.example: His mug appeared on the front page of every paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他的脸登上了每份报纸的头版。
senses.why: The face sense appeared in the eighteenth century, probably from the painted or exaggerated faces on drinking mugs, though the link is not certain.
senses.whyCN: 「脸」这个义项在十八世纪出现，可能来自酒杯上画着的夸张人脸，不过这一联系并不确定。

senses.title: To rob someone, especially in the street
senses.definition: to attack and rob a person, typically in a public place
senses.definitionCN: 袭击并抢走某人的财物，通常发生在公共场所
senses.example: A stranger tried to mug him near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 一个陌生人在车站附近试图抢他。
senses.why: The verb, recorded in the nineteenth century, may have grown from the face sense through the idea of striking someone in the face, but its origin is uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词十九世纪才有记录，可能经由「打脸」的想法从「脸」义长出来，但其来源不确定。

intro.en: Mug is a word of uncertain origin: the drinking vessel appears in the sixteenth century, the face sense in the eighteenth, and the verb to rob in the nineteenth.
intro.cn: mug 的词源不确定：杯子义见于十六世纪，脸义见于十八世纪，抢劫的动词义见于十九世纪。

items.en: No source is firmly established; the drinking-vessel sense is often said to come from a Scandinavian word, but this is not certain.
items.cn: 来源没有得到确证；一般认为杯子义可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语，但这并不确定。

items.en: Mug is recorded in the sixteenth century as a stout drinking cup, the sense that still anchors the word.
items.cn: mug 在十六世纪以「厚实的大杯」被记录下来，这个义项至今仍是词的中心。

items.en: An informal sense for the face appears in the eighteenth century, perhaps linked to faces painted on mugs, though the connection is uncertain.
items.cn: 「脸」的口语义项在十八世纪出现，可能与杯子上画的人脸有关，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: The verb meaning to rob or attack appears in the nineteenth century, possibly from striking someone's face, but its path is unclear.
items.cn: 表示抢劫或袭击的动词义在十九世纪出现，可能源自打人的脸，但其演变路径并不清楚。

items.en: Modern English mug covers the cup, its contents, a face and a street robbery, with mug shot and mugger as common extensions.
items.cn: 现代英语的 mug 兼指杯子、杯中物、脸与街头抢劫，并常见 mug shot 与 mugger 等扩展形式。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the mug stem, while the near-meaning group collects words for cups and for robbery.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 mug 词干上的形式，近义组收表示杯子与抢劫的词。

entries.definitionCN: 在公共场所袭击并抢劫他人的人。

entries.definitionCN: 一只大杯所能容纳的量。

entries.definitionCN: 警方留存的人脸照片；大头照。

entries.definition: A small open container used for drinking.
entries.definitionCN: 用于饮水的小型敞口容器。

entries.definition: A tall drinking glass without a handle.
entries.definitionCN: 高身无柄的饮水玻璃杯。

entries.definition: To take property from someone by force or threat.
entries.definitionCN: 以暴力或威胁夺取他人财物。

entries.definition: To take something that belongs to another person.

normalIntro.en: A plain word with three separate lives, the cup, the face and the robbery, all built on the same short shape.
normalIntro.cn: 这个朴素的词有三段彼此分开的经历：杯子、脸和抢劫，全都建立在同一个短小的词形上。

normal.en: The earliest recorded mug is a stout drinking cup of the sixteenth century.
normal.cn: 最早有记录的 mug 是十六世纪那种厚实的大杯。

normal.en: mugful adds -ful to mug, naming the amount that fills it.
normal.cn: mugful 在 mug 后加 -ful，指装满一杯的量。

normal.en: mug shot joins the face sense to shot, a photograph taken for the police.
normal.cn: mug shot 把「脸」义与 shot 结合，指警方拍下的照片。

normal.en: mugger and mugging come from the verb, adding -er for the person and -ing for the act.
normal.cn: mugger 与 mugging 来自动词，加 -er 指人，加 -ing 指行为。

normal.en: Because the vessel sense came first, the later senses look like slang growing out of a household object.
normal.cn: 因为杯子的义项最先出现，后来的义项看起来像从一件家常物件上长出来的俚语。

abstract.en: A cup, a face and a crime share one short word, and only the context tells them apart.
abstract.cn: 一只杯子、一张脸和一桩罪案共用一个短词，只有语境能把它们分开。

abstract.en: The handle on the mug is the small hook that makes the object easy to hold.
abstract.cn: 杯柄就是那个让人容易握住物件的小钩子。

abstract.en: A word can start on a kitchen table and end up in a police report.
abstract.cn: 一个词可以从厨房桌上开始，最后走进警方的记录里。

examples.cn: 她往一只厚实的陶瓷杯里倒满热茶。

intro.en: Ditch comes from Old English dic, a trench or dike, a word older than written English.
intro.cn: ditch 来自古英语 dic（沟、堤），这个词比有记载的英语还要早。

items.en: Dic meant a dug trench or a raised bank.
items.cn: dic 指挖出的沟或筑起的堤。

items.en: Farmers cut dics to lead water off wet fields.
items.cn: 农人挖沟把水从湿田里引走。

items.en: The spelling settled as dich and then ditch.
items.cn: 拼写先作 dich，后来固定为 ditch。

items.en: Roadside ditches became a common sight in law and travel.
items.cn: 路边沟在律法与时人游记里成了常见之物。

items.en: The verb appeared with the sense of getting rid of.
items.cn: 动词形式出现了「甩掉」的意思。

items.en: Today a pilot can ditch a plane and a person can ditch a habit.
items.cn: 今天飞机可以迫降，人也可以戒掉一个习惯。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a single starting sound, while the meaning group names other dug channels.
note.cn: 形近组只差开头一个音，近义组则是几种挖出来的通道。

branches.en: The first sense is the open cut in the ground.

definition_zh: 收养；采用；正式通过

senses.title: The legal taking of a child

senses.title: The taking up of a method

senses.title: A state that supports another
senses.definition: a country that has formally agreed to support another country, especially in war

senses.example: The island remained a loyal ally for over a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛国作为忠诚的盟国持续了一个多世纪。
senses.why: The word goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to bind'; an ally is a state bound to another by treaty, so the relationship is a tie rather than a mere friendship.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自拉丁语中意为「捆绑」的动词；ally 是被条约绑在另一国身边的国家，所以它描述的是一种约束关系，而不只是友好。

senses.title: A person who gives support
senses.definition: a person who helps or supports another in a dispute, campaign, or struggle

senses.example: She found a powerful ally in the local newspaper editor.
senses.exampleCN: 她争取到了当地报纸主编这个有力的支持者。
senses.why: Once the binding image leaves the battlefield, any person who stands with you becomes an ally, and the word keeps the sense of a commitment made in a contest.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「捆绑」的意象离开战场，任何站到你这一边的人都可以叫 ally；这个词仍保留着「在较量中立下承诺」的味道，所以比 supporter 更有阵营感。

senses.title: To join forces with

senses.example: The small parties allied themselves with the reformers.
senses.exampleCN: 这些小党与改革派联合起来。
senses.why: The verb makes the binding an act: the parties themselves do the tying, which is why it typically appears with with or oneself with.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「捆绑」变成动作：是各方自己动手把彼此系起来，所以它常与 with 连用，或用 ally oneself with 这种反身结构。

intro.en: Ally and alliance are two branches of one Latin verb for binding.

items.en: ligare meant 'to tie, bind', and it also underlies ligament and obligation.
items.cn: ligare 意为「系、捆、绑」，ligament 与 obligation 也由它而来。

items.en: alligare added ad- to give 'bind to', used of attaching one thing or person to another.
items.cn: alligare 加 ad- 表示「绑到……上」，用于把一物或一人系到另一物或另一人身上。

items.en: The French verb alier meant 'to unite, combine', and its participle alie gave the noun for a person or party so united.
items.cn: 法语动词 alier 意为「联合、结合」，其分词形式 alie 生出指「被联合的一方」的名词。

items.en: English borrowed ally in the fourteenth century, first for a person joined to another by marriage or treaty.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 ally，最初指因婚姻或条约而与另一方结合的人。

items.en: Warfare fixed the state sense, and the capitalised Allies names the coalition that fought in the two world wars.
items.cn: 战争固定了「国家」这一义项；首字母大写的 Allies 特指两次世界大战中的同盟国阵营。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin binding root; the near-meaning group grades partners by the strength of the tie.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「捆绑」词根；近义组按关系紧密程度排列伙伴。

normalIntro.en: Ally is the partner in a binding: a state, a supporter, or the act of joining.
normalIntro.cn: ally 是「捆绑」中的一方：一个国家、一个支持者，或结盟这个动作。

normal.en: The noun is countable: an ally, two allies.
normal.cn: 名词可数：an ally，复数 allies。

normal.en: The verb takes with: ally with a neighbouring state.
normal.cn: 动词接 with：ally with a neighbouring state。

normal.en: Ally ends in a single l, alliance has two.
normal.cn: ally 只有一个 l，alliance 有两个。

normal.en: Allied is the adjective, as in allied forces.
normal.cn: 形容词是 allied，如 allied forces。

normal.en: With a capital A, the Allies means the wartime coalition.
normal.cn: 首字母大写时，the Allies 指战时的同盟国阵营。

examples.en: The country has been a reliable ally for thirty years.

examples.en: Small businesses allied with the union to oppose the new tax.
examples.cn: 小企业与工会联合起来反对这项新税。

examples.en: He proved an unexpected ally when the vote turned against her.
examples.cn: 表决对她不利时，他成了意想不到的支持者。
